processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: A 100 g alloy ingot prepared by cold-crucible levitation melting (99.99% pure Fe, 99.9% Mn, 99.9% Al, 99.9% Cr, 99.8% high-purity graphite) was remelted by induction melting and poured into a copper mold rotating at 600 rpm; as-cast steel strips of 80 mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm were obtained.
As-cast strips were stress relief annealed at 400 °C for 1 h prior to cold rolling.

Cold rolled with 20% reduction achieved by multipass rolling on a twin roll mill (Φ160), denoted 'CR20%'. The 20% reduction eliminates some micropores caused by solidification shrinkage and avoids great influence on the structure of the steel strips.

structures.overall_structure: Cold-rolled (CR20%) near-rapidly solidified low-density Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-6Cr steel strip. The constituent phases are still γ-austenite and δ-ferrite with ordered DO3 phase after cold rolling, completely consistent with the as-cast steel strips. Irregularly shaped δ-ferrite distributes in the γ-austenite matrix; Cr addition makes the short rod-shape ferrite change into block/vermicular ferrite, and cold rolling does not significantly change the morphology or volume fraction of δ-ferrite. Nano-scale κ-carbides precipitate in the austenite and ordered DO3 phase in the δ-ferrite.
structures.number_of_phases: 3 (γ-austenite, δ-ferrite, ordered DO3; plus nano-scale κ-carbide in austenite)

precipitates.type: ordered DO3 phase (BCC, lattice parameter a = 0.565 nm)

defects.type: {111} planar slip bands, average spacing 45 ± 13 nm

defect_interactions.interaction_type: high-density slip bands blocking dislocation movement
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: There is a higher density of slip bands in the Cr-containing cold-rolled steel strips than in the Cr-free cold-rolled steel strips. The high-density slip bands significantly block the movement of dislocations and increase the deformation difficulty, which leads to an increase in strength of the Cr-containing steel strips. The smaller the slip band spacing, the greater the stress required for deformation.

interfaces.slip_behavior: {111} planar slip bands are present in the austenite of the CR20% steel strips. The average spacing of the slip bands in the CR20% 6Cr steel strip is 45 ± 13 nm, smaller than the Cr-free (371 ± 47 nm) and 3Cr (100 ± 15 nm) strips, giving a stronger reinforcement effect after cold rolling.
interfaces.phase_evolution: The constituent phases remain γ-austenite and δ-ferrite with ordered DO3 phase after cold rolling, completely consistent with the as-cast steel strips.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gage width 4 mm, gage length 12 mm; specimens machined from the steel strips
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile tests performed at least 3 times by a MTS Criterion 44 Mechanical Property Tester.
Derived from true stress-strain / strain hardening rate curves (Fig. 9c).

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: ultimate tensile strength after 20% cold rolling (1264 MPa for CR20% 6Cr vs 1154 MPa for CR20% 0Cr)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku D/Max-2200, Cu target operated at 40 kV and 40 mA, graphite monochromator, λ = 0.154056 nm
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification of the as-cast and cold-rolled steel strips
characterization_methods.key_findings: The constituent phases are still γ-austenite and δ-ferrite with ordered DO3 phase after cold rolling, completely consistent with the as-cast steel strips. A double-peak between 43.5° and 45.0° in the as-cast strip corresponds to (110)δ and (220)DO3.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Phenom Pro; after mechanical polishing and etching (3.3 vol% nitric acid, 3.3 vol% acetic acid, 0.1 vol% hydrofluoric acid; etching time 3 s)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SEM photographs taken at a position of 0.5 mm from the strip surface along the thickness direction
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterization of microstructure and δ-ferrite morphology/volume fraction
characterization_methods.key_findings: Irregularly shaped δ-ferrite distributes in the γ-austenite matrix; Cr addition changes short rod-shaped ferrite into block ferrite. Volume fraction of δ-ferrite in the cold-rolled strips is 5%, 12% and 18% for 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr. Cold rolling causes no significant change in δ-ferrite morphology/volume fraction.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL-2010F operated at 200 kV; specimens prepared by twin-jet electrolytic polishing at −30 °C and 30 V in a mixed solution of 10% perchloric acid and 90% alcohol
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine nano-scale precipitated phases and deformation microstructures (slip bands)
characterization_methods.key_findings: {111} planar slip bands are present in the austenite of the CR20% steel strips; average slip band spacing in the CR20% 6Cr strip is 45 ± 13 nm (0Cr 371 ± 47 nm, 3Cr 100 ± 15 nm). The superlattice reflection intensity of the γ-austenite κ-carbide is barely visible in the as-cast 6Cr strip.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature; at least 3 tests; gage width 4 mm, gage length 12 mm; constant strain rate 2.5 × 10^-4 s^-1; per GB/T-228.1-2010
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure mechanical properties of the steel strips
characterization_methods.key_findings: After cold rolling, UTS is 1154 MPa, 1270 MPa and 1264 MPa for CR20% 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr; elongation remains about 21% for the Cr-containing cold-rolled strips.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: AccuPyc II 1340 Gas Displacement Density Analyzer
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure average density of the steel strips
characterization_methods.key_findings: Measured average density of the 6Cr steel strips is 6.66 g/cm3 (0Cr 6.71 g/cm3, 3Cr 6.69 g/cm3).

characterization_methods.technique: Chemical composition analysis (ICP-MS and combustion infrared)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP) and CS2800 carbon-sulfur analyzer
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure chemical composition of the steel strips

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: average phase fraction measured in ten different positions
characterization_methods.key_findings: δ-ferrite volume fraction in the cold-rolled strips is 5%, 12% and 18% (0Cr, 3Cr, 6Cr).

unmapped_findings: Measured composition of the 6Cr steel strip (wt.%): Mn 20.18, Al 9.12, C 1.20, Cr 6.08, S 0.0011, Fe Bal. (Table 1).
Measured average density of the 6Cr steel strip is 6.66 g/cm3 (0Cr 6.71 g/cm3, 3Cr 6.69 g/cm3).
The 0.5 mm from strip surface along the thickness direction was the SEM photography position for microstructure characterization.

As-cast 6Cr condition (not CR20%): the DO3 phase precipitated in the δ-ferrite has a size of 28 ± 4 nm, with no significant change in DO3 size compared with the 3Cr strip; measured lattice parameter of the κ-carbides and γ-austenite is 0.389 nm and 0.384 nm, respectively.

XRD of the CR20% strips: the constituent phases are still γ-austenite and δ-ferrite with ordered DO3 phase after cold rolling, completely consistent with the as-cast steel strips; after further annealing the double-peak changes to a single-peak between 43.5° and 45.0°.
Strain hardening rates of the CR20% steel strips decrease gradually with increasing strain; addition of Cr increases the strain hardening rate of the CR20% steel strips (Fig. 9c, text block b0065).

Annealing the cold-rolled strips (CR20% + annealed, a separate condition) has no significant effect on the yield strength/UTS relative to CR20%, attributed to the high-density slip bands becoming the main strengthening factor.
